title: Finite type modules on a ringed space: stable under epimorphic images and extensions (Stacks 01B7)
statement: Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space (for instance a scheme [def-pc-scheme] with its structure sheaf) and $\mathit{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ the abelian category of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules on the open sets of $X$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. An $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ is *of finite type* if every point $x\in X$ has an open neighbourhood $U$ and finitely many sections $s_1,\dots,s_n\in\mathcal F(U)$ such that the associated map $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal F|_U$, $e_i\mapsto s_i$, is an epimorphism of $\mathcal O_U$-modules ([def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation] (1); on a scheme this is the notion of [pqf-def-coherent] (2)). Then: (1) if $p:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ is an epimorphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules and $\mathcal F$ is of finite type, then $\mathcal G$ is of finite type (in particular the image $\operatorname{Im}\varphi=\operatorname{Ker}(\mathcal H\to\operatorname{Coker}\varphi)$ of a morphism $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal H$ whose source is of finite type is of finite type); (2) if $0\to\mathcal F_1\to\mathcal F_2\to\mathcal F_3\to0$ is a short exact sequence of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] and $\mathcal F_1$ and $\mathcal F_3$ are of finite type, then $\mathcal F_2$ is of finite type.

proof.text: Generation tested on sections. Let $U\subseteq X$ be open and $s_1,\dots,s_n\in\mathcal F(U)$. The map $\sigma:\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal F|_U$, $e_i\mapsto s_i$ [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation], sends $(a_1,\dots,a_n)\in\mathcal O_X(W)^{\oplus n}$, $W\subseteq U$ open, to $\sum_ia_is_i|_W$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-space-module-exactness-local-lifting] (1) on the ringed space $(U,\mathcal O_U)$, whose opens are the opens $W\subseteq U$ of $X$: $\sigma$ is an epimorphism of $\mathcal O_U$-modules if and only if (*) for every open $W\subseteq U$ and every $t\in\mathcal F(W)$ there are an open covering $W=\bigcup_kW_k$ and $a_{ik}\in\mathcal O_X(W_k)$ with $t|_{W_k}=\sum_ia_{ik}s_i|_{W_k}$. Likewise, by the same lemma (1) on $X$, a morphism $p:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules is an epimorphism if and only if for every open $W$ and $t\in\mathcal G(W)$ there are a covering $W=\bigcup_kW_k$ and $f_k\in\mathcal F(W_k)$ with $p(f_k)=t|_{W_k}$. Throughout, morphisms of $\mathcal O_X$-modules are $\mathcal O_X(W)$-linear on sections and commute with restriction [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

source.place: Modules, Definition 01B5 (label definition-finite-type, line 810); Section 01AF (label section-kernels)

proof.text: Part (1). Let $p:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ be an epimorphism and $\mathcal F$ of finite type; let $x\in X$. Choose an open $U\ni x$ and $s_1,\dots,s_n\in\mathcal F(U)$ whose map $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal F|_U$ is an epimorphism [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation] (1). We check (*) of step 1 for the sections $p(s_1),\dots,p(s_n)\in\mathcal G(U)$. Let $W\subseteq U$ be open and $t\in\mathcal G(W)$. Since $p$ is an epimorphism, step 1 gives a covering $W=\bigcup_kW_k$ and $f_k\in\mathcal F(W_k)$ with $p(f_k)=t|_{W_k}$. Since the $s_i$ generate, step 1 (*) gives for each $k$ a covering $W_k=\bigcup_lW_{kl}$ and $a_{ikl}\in\mathcal O_X(W_{kl})$ with $f_k|_{W_{kl}}=\sum_ia_{ikl}s_i|_{W_{kl}}$. Applying $p$, which is linear and commutes with restriction, $t|_{W_{kl}}=p(f_k)|_{W_{kl}}=\sum_ia_{ikl}\,p(s_i)|_{W_{kl}}$, and the $W_{kl}$ cover $W$. By step 1 the map $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal G|_U$, $e_i\mapsto p(s_i)$, is an epimorphism; as $x$ was arbitrary, $\mathcal G$ is of finite type. This is 'the statement on images is trivial' of the source.

proof.text: Part (1), the image. Let $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal H$ with $\mathcal F$ of finite type, $\pi:\mathcal H\to\operatorname{Coker}\varphi$ its cokernel in the abelian category $\mathit{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-sp-abelian], and $i:\mathcal I\to\mathcal H$ a kernel of $\pi$, which is the image $\operatorname{Im}\varphi$ [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]. Since $\pi\varphi=0$ there is a unique $\varphi':\mathcal F\to\mathcal I$ with $i\varphi'=\varphi$. The complex $\mathcal F\xrightarrow{\varphi}\mathcal H\xrightarrow{\pi}\operatorname{Coker}\varphi$ is exact at $\mathcal H$, since $\operatorname{Im}\varphi$ is by definition $\operatorname{Ker}\pi$; so $\varphi'$ is an epimorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-exact-iff-epi-kernel-lift], and $\mathcal I$ is of finite type by step 2.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01B7 (label lemma-extension-finite-type, line 855) and its proof (first assertion: the image of a morphism of finite type modules)

proof.text: Part (2), choice of local generators. Let $0\to\mathcal F_1\xrightarrow{f}\mathcal F_2\xrightarrow{g}\mathcal F_3\to0$ be short exact with $\mathcal F_1,\mathcal F_3$ of finite type, and $x\in X$. By [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation] (1) there are opens $U_1,U_3\ni x$, sections $t_1,\dots,t_m\in\mathcal F_1(U_1)$ and $u_1,\dots,u_n\in\mathcal F_3(U_3)$ whose maps $\mathcal O_{U_1}^{\oplus m}\to\mathcal F_1|_{U_1}$ and $\mathcal O_{U_3}^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal F_3|_{U_3}$ are epimorphisms. Sections of $\mathcal F_3$ lift locally: $g$ is an epimorphism [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence], so by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-space-module-exactness-local-lifting] (1) each $u_j$ has, on a member $W_j\ni x$ of an open covering of $U_3$, a section $v_j\in\mathcal F_2(W_j)$ with $g(v_j)=u_j|_{W_j}$. Put $U=U_1\cap U_3\cap W_1\cap\dots\cap W_n$, an open neighbourhood of $x$ (a finite intersection), and let $\Psi:\mathcal O_U^{\oplus m}\oplus\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal F_2|_U$ be the map of the $m+n$ sections $f(t_1)|_U,\dots,f(t_m)|_U,v_1|_U,\dots,v_n|_U\in\mathcal F_2(U)$.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01B7 (label lemma-extension-finite-type, line 855) and its proof ('sections of F_3 locally lift to sections of F_2')

proof.text: Part (2), $\Psi$ is an epimorphism. We check (*) of step 1 for these $m+n$ sections. Let $W\subseteq U$ be open and $s\in\mathcal F_2(W)$. (a) Since $W\subseteq U_3$ and the $u_j$ generate $\mathcal F_3|_{U_3}$, step 1 (*) gives a covering $W=\bigcup_kW_k$ and $a_{jk}\in\mathcal O_X(W_k)$ with $g(s)|_{W_k}=\sum_ja_{jk}u_j|_{W_k}$. Then $r_k:=s|_{W_k}-\sum_ja_{jk}v_j|_{W_k}\in\mathcal F_2(W_k)$ satisfies $g(r_k)=g(s)|_{W_k}-\sum_ja_{jk}u_j|_{W_k}=0$, using that $g$ is linear, commutes with restriction and $g(v_j)=u_j|_{W_j}$ with $W_k\subseteq W_j$. (b) The complex $\mathcal F_1\xrightarrow{f}\mathcal F_2\xrightarrow{g}\mathcal F_3$ is exact at $\mathcal F_2$ ($\operatorname{Im}f=\operatorname{Ker}g$, part of the definition of a short exact sequence [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]), so by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-space-module-exactness-local-lifting] (2) there are a covering $W_k=\bigcup_lW_{kl}$ and $c_{kl}\in\mathcal F_1(W_{kl})$ with $f(c_{kl})=r_k|_{W_{kl}}$. (c) Since $W_{kl}\subseteq U_1$ and the $t_i$ generate $\mathcal F_1|_{U_1}$, step 1 (*) gives a covering $W_{kl}=\bigcup_qW_{klq}$ and $b_{iklq}\in\mathcal O_X(W_{klq})$ with $c_{kl}|_{W_{klq}}=\sum_ib_{iklq}t_i|_{W_{klq}}$. (d) On $W_{klq}$, applying the linear map $f$: $s|_{W_{klq}}=r_k|_{W_{klq}}+\sum_ja_{jk}|_{W_{klq}}v_j|_{W_{klq}}=\sum_ib_{iklq}f(t_i)|_{W_{klq}}+\sum_ja_{jk}|_{W_{klq}}v_j|_{W_{klq}}$, and the $W_{klq}$ cover $W$. By step 1, $\Psi$ is an epimorphism of $\mathcal O_U$-modules; so every $x$ has a neighbourhood on which $\mathcal F_2$ is generated by finitely many sections, i.e. $\mathcal F_2$ is of finite type [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation] (1). (This is the source's 'corresponding result in the category of modules over a ring': the generators of the submodule together with lifts of generators of the quotient generate the module, carried out on sections over the members of a covering instead of on stalks.)

split_report.summary: Split following Stacks 01B7 (modules.tex line 855) and its proof, read with Definition 01B5. Five elementary steps: (1) generation by finitely many sections tested on sections over a covering, from the existing same-unit lemma lem-weil-pbc-ringed-space-module-exactness-local-lifting (1) on (U,O_U); (2) clause (1): images of generators along an epimorphism generate ('trivial' in the source, written out with two refinements of coverings); (3) the image of a morphism with finite type source, via the cokernel and lem-weil-pbc-abelian-exact-iff-epi-kernel-lift, as the citers use it; (4)-(5) clause (2): sections of F_3 locally lift (local-lifting (1)), and the kernel of g is locally in the image of f (local-lifting (2)), so the generators of F_1 and the lifts of those of F_3 generate F_2 over a small open; the source's 'result for modules over a ring applied to stalks' is carried out on sections over coverings, which avoids stalks and any new node. Statement: kept, with the finite type notion now cited to def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation (1) (pqf-def-coherent is for schemes only) and the image made explicit as Ker(H -> Coker). No new nodes. Mathlib: SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType exists (definition only), recorded as mathlib_candidate; no lemma for images or extensions.
